title: Delivery
description: v0.10 (`dependencyDrawing`: one optional, capped Muse Image drawing of a small part of the tree, served only if its read-back matched the analyzer exactly; additive, old records stay valid and simply lack it) v0.9 (`dependencyTree`: the analyzer's call, copy and job links, recorded as soon as analysis finishes; additive, old records stay valid and simply lack it) v0.8 (`ciNotAdded`: GitHub refused the re-verify workflow file, so the pull request went out without it; additive) v0.7 (a delivery that stops because nothing can be converted lists up to 30 skipped and refused programs as skipped, each with its reason; additive, old records stay valid) (v0.6 buildCheck: optional whole-repository build verdict and counts, a summary of build-report.schema.json; old records stay valid) (v0.5 (create-target: optional createTarget and targetCreated; old records stay valid) (v0.4 convert-anyway: per-program assurance, top-level convertAnyway, repoMaxUsd and spentUsd; old records stay valid) (v0.3 target optional: a visitor's import keeps its results on the site; adds public and per-program reason). A migration from a legacy GitHub repository to a pull request on a target repository, as served by services/api GET /deliveries/{id}. Updated while it runs.

target.description: Repository that receives the pull request; null for an import whose results stay on the site. With createTarget it is the repository that is to be created (see targetCreated).

createTarget.description: Present when the delivery was asked to create its own target repository (admin or local command line only)

targetCreated.description: true once this delivery created the target repository (createTarget set). false or absent: nothing was created, for example before the delivery stage, after a refusal, or in --dry-run.

error.description: Why the delivery stopped, cut to 500 characters. An error that starts with 'no convertible programs' means it stopped after analysis, before any model call: a refusal, not an engine fault (the dashboard relies on this prefix). Its counts cover every refused program, while `programs` lists at most the first 30 skipped and refused programs.

buildCheck.description: Whole-repository build check of the delivered programs (contracts/build-report.schema.json): the verdict, one sentence per cause, and counts. A failing build check never blocks the delivery of programs that are certified on their own; the pull request body says so. The full report is build/build-report.json in the pull request.

dependencyTree.description: Additive (v0.9). The analyzer's dependency links for this repository (contracts/analysis-report.schema.json `dependencies`), recorded as soon as analysis finishes, before any conversion and whether or not anything can be converted. Only kinds call, copy and job; each distinct {from, to, kind} once, in analyzer order. No model is involved. Labels come from the imported repository and are untrusted: render them as text. Absent or null: an older delivery, or one that stopped before analysis finished.

total.description: Distinct links the analyzer reported, before the cap

truncated.description: true when `total` is above the cap of 1000: `edges` holds the first 1000 in analyzer order, and any impact computed from them may miss names

dependencyDrawing.description: Additive (v0.10). One Muse Image drawing of one small part of dependencyTree, off unless the engine sets TREE_IMAGE_MODEL_ID. Written by its own job to tree-drawing.json beside delivery.json and merged in by GET /deliveries/{id}. It never fails or delays a delivery. Muse Wonder reads the picture back without seeing the graph, and code compares that with the analyzer's links. Only status `passed` has a drawing, at GET /deliveries/{id}/dependency-drawing. A pass is not a proof and a rejection does not show the drawing was wrong; the analyzer's tree is the source of truth. Absent or null: off, or an older delivery.

status.description: failed: at least one image went to the read-back and none passed (or the read-back could not be used). not-drawn: no image reached a read-back; `reason` says why.

reason.description: A fixed word, never text from a repository, a model or a provider

verified.description: true only with status passed: exact match of boxes and arrows, ignoring case and surrounding spaces

part.description: What was drawn: the first name in analyzer order with 2 to 8 links of its own and labels matching the strict label pattern, upper-cased. Never a whole repository.

imageTokens.description: Muse Image's usage as returned, numbers only

imagesDrawn.description: Images requested for this delivery, counted before each call. Muse Image's price is not published, so images are counted and not priced.

readCostUsd.description: Estimated read-back spend at the list price; a cap of $0.15 per delivery. Excludes Muse Image.

precheck.description: Visitor imports only: the compile-only check of the original programs (contracts/compile-check.schema.json). checked = programs asked; stopped = why the check ended early (sandbox busy or unreachable, time or count bound) or null; notes = fixed phrases only (never output of a subprocess, the sandbox or a program; raw details stay in the server-side deliver.log).

run.description: Live summary of the converter run: status, stage, recent events, efficiency so far

costUsd.description: Convert-anyway: this program's estimated model spend (null: no price known)

assurance.description: Convert-anyway mode: what the verifier could and could not show. Only `certified` is certified; status stays not-certified for the others. The run record has the details.

reason.description: Why a program was skipped (for example: over the line limit for visitor imports, or the analyzer's notConvertibleReason when nothing in the repository can be converted)

public.description: Started by a visitor without the admin passcode (sandboxed, capped, never opens a pull request)

convertAnyway.description: Convert-anyway mode was on (admin path or local CLI only, never a visitor import): programs that would be refused are translated and compile-checked, and labelled by assurance

repoMaxUsd.description: REPO_MAX_USD: hard cap on model spend across all programs of this delivery (convert-anyway mode)

ciNotAdded.description: Additive (v0.8). Why the pull request has no re-verify CI: the push token may not write workflow files. Absent or null: the CI was added, or the target already has it.

spentUsd.description: Model spend so far across the programs of this delivery (estimated, list prices; null if a model has no known price)

request.description: POST /deliveries body. With the admin passcode: any allowed target, pull request opened. Without it (a visitor): legacy only, any public GitHub repository, sandboxed and capped; results stay on the site.

target.description: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> that receives the pull request (admin only)

convertAnyway.description: Admin only: a visitor request that sets it is refused (403)

createTarget.description: Admin only (a visitor request that sets it is refused, 403): create a new repository for the result and open the pull request into it. Mutually exclusive with target. Never reuses an existing repository.
Ask the delivery to create its target repository. The owner must be on the same owner allowlist as any target (DIOCLE_IMPORT_OWNERS); the repository must not exist yet.

name.description: Repository name: 1 to 100 of letters, digits, '.', '-', '_'; not '.' or '..'

owner.description: Account that will own it. Omitted or null: the GitHub user the engine is logged in as (gh).

visibility.description: Private unless public is asked for explicitly
